requirement: Investigate whether ADD's (and siblings') 'operands do not type-check together' failure is caused by an inadequate type system, and if so, design a safe fix without weakening type safety globally.

mechanismConfirmedByDirectSourceRead.typeInferenceIsCorrect: lib/contract-model/ir/type-check.ts's inferType(expr) (lines 23-149) is a sound, conservative type-checker: every composite kind (ADD/SUM lines 42-55, MULTIPLY 56-71, SUBTRACT 72-78, DIVIDE 79-86, MAX/MIN 87-96, COMPARE 97-103, AND/OR 104-110, NOT 111-115, IF 116-124, DURING_PERIOD 129-132, SCHEDULE 133-141, EVENT_ACTIVE 142-148) checks its own operands' inferred types and returns UNSUPPORTED_TYPE the instant ANY operand is itself unsupported (the isUnsupported() guard, e.g. line 45) or the operands' types are not mutually compatible (e.g. line 52's RATIO/MONEY exclusivity, line 122's IF-branch-type-mismatch). This is CORRECT, INTENTIONAL, and SAFE behavior for the question inferType is actually answering: 'can this composite's OWN, TOP-LEVEL VALUE be assigned one clean scalar type?' An ADD of (MONEY, MONEY, UNSUPPORTED) genuinely has no well-defined top-level scalar sum - that verdict must not be relaxed, or the compiler would silently fabricate a fake computed total for a partially-unknown addition (a false-executability regression the mission explicitly prohibits).
mechanismConfirmedByDirectSourceRead.theRealDefectIsInMaterialization_NOT_typ: The defect is one layer up, in lib/contract-model/compiler/semantic/normalize.ts's buildComposite (lines 94-99). buildComposite receives `fields` (already-recursively-normalized child IRExpression nodes - normalize.ts:168's operands.map(normalizeExpression) runs BEFORE buildComposite is called) and calls inferType(draft) on the assembled parent. When inferType returns UNSUPPORTED_TYPE (line 97), buildComposite does `return unsupportedNode(ctx, unsupportedMessage, wire, prov)` - and unsupportedNode (lines 70-80ish, confirmed via search) constructs a FRESH, FLAT IRUnsupportedExpression carrying only sourceEvidence/semanticDescription/reason strings. The `draft` object - which contains the FULL, ALREADY-BUILT `fields` (e.g. the entire `operands` array of already-normalized IRExpression children, most of which may be perfectly well-typed) - is discarded in its entirety at this return statement. Nothing about inferType's answer required this discard; inferType only said 'the PARENT's own scalar type is unknown,' not 'throw away everything you know about the parent's children.'
mechanismConfirmedByDirectSourceRead.conflationIdentified: buildComposite conflates two genuinely distinct facts that the current IRUnsupportedExpression schema (lib/contract-model/ir/types.ts:399-404, fields: kind/type/sourceEvidence/semanticDescription/reason/requiredReview/provenance/exprId) has no way to keep separate: (1) 'this composite's own value cannot be safely typed/executed' (true, and must remain true - this is the safety-critical fact) and (2) 'nothing is known about this composite's internal substructure' (false in every ledger row examined in 01 except the fully-truncated A3/Maintenance-EBITDA and A6/Invoice-Restrictions cases - in every poison-propagation case, MOST of the composite's operands DID successfully normalize and type-check).

isThisATypeSystemGap.verdict: PARTIAL - narrowly, yes, but not in inferType's own logic.
isThisATypeSystemGap.reasoning: The type CHECKING rules (inferType) are not inadequate and must not change - they correctly compute 'is this composite as a whole cleanly typed.' What IS inadequate is the IR's REPRESENTATION SCHEMA for the 'partially typed, partially not' case: IRUnsupportedExpression (types.ts:399-404) has no field for 'the attempted structure that produced this UNSUPPORTED verdict.' This is a narrow, additive schema gap - not a flaw in the type-checking algorithm, and not a case for relaxing any type-safety rule. The fix is: give IRUnsupportedExpression an OPTIONAL field that losslessly carries the already-built child structure (the very same `fields`/`draft` object buildComposite currently discards), so a downstream consumer (deterministic completeness-check, the independent verifier, a human reviewer) can see 'this composite has 20 operands, 18 of them are well-typed real IR nodes (METRIC_REFERENCE / DEFINED_TERM_REFERENCE / MULTIPLY(PERCENT,...) etc.), exactly 2 are genuinely UNSUPPORTED leaves, and THAT is why the top-level composite itself is honestly marked UNSUPPORTED' - rather than the current 'the entire thing is one opaque UNSUPPORTED blob with no visible substructure.'

safeFixDesign.principle: Additive-only. type stays exactly `null` on the UNSUPPORTED wrapper (never widened to accept a partial/optimistic type) - so NOTHING downstream can accidentally treat a poisoned composite as executable. Only a new, optional, purely-diagnostic field is added.
safeFixDesign.proposedSchemaChange: Add an optional `attemptedStructure?: IRExpression` field to IRUnsupportedExpression (types.ts:399-404). When buildComposite (normalize.ts:97) discards a composite because inferType(draft) === UNSUPPORTED_TYPE, it constructs the unsupportedNode as today (type: null, same reason/sourceEvidence/semanticDescription) but ALSO attaches `attemptedStructure: draft as unknown as IRExpression` - i.e. the fully-assembled composite exactly as it would have been emitted had it type-checked, kind/operands/left/right/etc. and all, still individually typed at each surviving leaf/subtree. Because `attemptedStructure` sits OUTSIDE the closed `IRExpression` discriminated union's normal traversal paths (it is a diagnostic sidecar on an UNSUPPORTED node, not a new expression kind other code paths must learn to interpret as executable), no existing consumer of calculationExpression/capacityExpression trees needs to change to remain safe - a consumer that ignores the new field behaves EXACTLY as it does today (sees kind=UNSUPPORTED, type=null, stops). Only code that is deliberately updated to read `attemptedStructure` (the intra-definition completeness check, extended per Unit A's implementation plan in 04) gains new capability; nothing gains new EXECUTABILITY.
safeFixDesign.whyNotWidenTheCompositeTypeItself: Rejected: giving ADD/SUM/etc.'s own `type` field an UNSUPPORTED_TYPE option (types.ts:274-313 etc. currently `type: "MONEY" | "NUMBER" | "RATIO"`, a closed union) would mean EVERY existing consumer that switches on a composite's `type` to decide how to evaluate it would need an new branch to avoid mishandling a now-possible UNSUPPORTED value flowing through a node it previously assumed was always executable - a much larger blast radius and a real risk of introducing a false-executability path if any single consumer's new branch is written wrong. The IRUnsupportedExpression-sidecar approach instead keeps the closed-world safety invariant ('if you see kind!=UNSUPPORTED, the node IS executable') fully intact.
safeFixDesign.whyNotASchemaMigration: This is additive (one new optional field on one existing interface), not a migration - no existing persisted IR document becomes invalid, no existing field changes meaning, and every existing reader that does not know about the new field continues to behave identically. This satisfies the mission's 'do not introduce schema migration unless truly unavoidable' constraint by not requiring one.

secondaryChangeRequired.change: Pass the fully-assembled `draft` through to unsupportedNode() as the new attemptedStructure payload instead of discarding it, when and only when computed === UNSUPPORTED_TYPE.
secondaryChangeRequired.typeCheckTsChangeRequired: NONE. inferType's logic is unchanged - it continues to answer exactly the question it answers today, exactly as conservatively. This is a normalization-layer (materialization) fix only.

conclusion: Not IR_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION_REQUIRED, not a global type-safety weakening. This is a bounded, additive, safety-preserving fix to how a failed composite's diagnostic node is MATERIALIZED, isolated entirely to normalize.ts's buildComposite plus one new optional field on IRUnsupportedExpression. See 04 for the full architecture decision and implementation scope.
